columns.label: Ebook
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily get and consume ebooks on the platform (free or paid) as a first-class product, open, buy, borrow, or read without hunting.

columns.label: Short-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily consume short-form video as a first-class surface (For You, Reels, Shorts).

columns.label: Long-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch creator / UGC long-form video (or specialty long video) as a core surface. Course lectures belong under Courses. Hollywood catalogs belong under Series/Films.

columns.label: Series/Films
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch series and films as an SVOD / catalog entertainment product.

columns.label: Courses
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily take or browse structured courses as a first-class product.

columns.label: Newsletters
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily read or subscribe to newsletters / creator writing as a first-class product.

columns.label: Audio
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily listen to music, podcasts, or audiobooks as a first-class product.

columns.label: Memberships
columns.definition: Yes if a creator or seller can accept payments from others and make money through the platform, checkout, fan subscriptions, tips, ads, shop, or creator funds. Not only a classic Patreon-style membership product.

columns.label: Community & Messaging
columns.definition: Yes if you can create or join a group, community, or club, including group chats, Groups, subreddits, community tabs, discussion boards, or community feeds. A one-off comment on a single video or listing is not the bar; a durable place for the group to talk is.

columns.label: Storefronts
columns.definition: Yes if the product gives a creator a custom storefront or site that can take the place of building their own website (bio page, creator site, branded shop). Not a shop tab on someone else’s multi-seller marketplace.

columns.label: Marketplaces
columns.definition: Yes if a typical person can search and shop a catalog of offerings from many sellers, courses, books, digital goods, etc. Storefront software (Shopify, WooCommerce) is not a marketplace unless shoppers browse many sellers there.

scaleFacts: Founded in 2019 by CEO Nadia Odunayo; independent, Black woman–owned alternative to Amazon-owned Goodreads.
Reportedly 4M+ users, driven by readers seeking a cleaner, more data-centric way to track and discover books.
Core tracker workflow: import Goodreads data; track read / currently reading / owned / DNF; reading goals; reviews; To-Read Pile.
Differentiation via structured metadata, mood, pacing, genre, page count, themes, content warnings, and character/story tags that feed recommendations and analytics.

strengths.title: Personalized discovery beyond star ratings
strengths.detail: Readers can seek books by how they want a book to feel, hopeful, dark, emotional, fast-paced, character-driven, not only by broad genre or popularity.

strengths.title: Excellent reading analytics
strengths.detail: Visual graphs and reports reveal reading patterns over time: genres, moods, formats, page counts, rating behavior, and reading pace.

strengths.title: Independent and ad-free alternative
strengths.detail: Black woman–owned, Amazon-free, no-ad positioning appeals to readers who want an alternative to Goodreads and a less commercially driven reading space.

strengths.title: Granular tracking tools
strengths.detail: Statuses for DNF and owned, quarter-star ratings, edition/format tracking, and reader- or author-submitted content warnings, more precision than a basic shelf model.

weaknesses.title: Smaller social layer than Goodreads
weaknesses.detail: Primarily personal tracking and recommendation; less-developed public discussion, groups, author-following, quote-sharing, review replies, and messaging than Goodreads.

weaknesses.title: Limited author and publisher tooling
weaknesses.detail: No formal Author Program or author-controlled profile management; authors generally cannot directly edit author or book pages.

weaknesses.title: Recommendation depth partly paywalled
weaknesses.detail: Free users get the core tracker and some recommendations; unlimited personalized recommendations and several advanced tools require StoryGraph Plus.

weaknesses.title: Smaller network effects
weaknesses.detail: About 4M+ users is substantial but far smaller than Goodreads, fewer friend connections, reviews, and social signals for obscure titles.

content:
Kahana is a library of curated hubs, Explore, Clubs, and optional Stripe. The StoryGraph is independent, Amazon-free book tracking and discovery, log books, visualize reading habits, and get mood/pace/genre-based recommendations. They overlap in places and diverge in others.

What each one is

Kahana is built around hubs people can open, Explore so strangers can find them, Aura as scarce daily recognition, and Clubs so discussion outlives a feed. Selling stays optional.

The StoryGraph is an independent, Amazon-free book tracking and discovery platform that helps readers log books, visualize reading habits, and find personalized recommendations based on mood, pace, genre, and other detailed attributes. Official site.

Why this comparison

This article puts Kahana and The StoryGraph side by side. It covers what each supports as a first-class product job, key features, and a few research notes so you have a clearer picture of what they are, how they compare, and what you can actually do on each one. It is not a teardown, and it is not a switch-tomorrow pitch.
contentAfter:
What you can do on each

On Kahana you can publish a hub, list it on Explore, discuss it in a Club, grant Aura, and turn on a Stripe paywall when you are ready to charge.

On The StoryGraph you can use Ebook as a first-class product job. You need a dedicated reader, a giant store, or social tracking of everything you have ever read.

Using Kahana with The StoryGraph

You can use both. The StoryGraph keeps doing what it already does well. Kahana is another place to package the work, get discovered, and grow an audience.

Keep the reader or tracker you already use. Put the Club pick, discussion questions, and related files on Kahana so the book is a shared library item, not only a private progress bar.
